As the new school year begins, a growing number of Americans support an outright ban on students using phones in the classroom.

The new school year is underway, and the call to ban iPhones in schools continues to grow louder.

That's right—although it's still July, summer seems to have ended early. My kids are heading back to school today and tomorrow, marking the second summer in a row that the first day of classes no longer falls in August.

Apple is marking the new school year with its annual "Back to School" promotion. Eligible students and educators who purchase selected Mac and iPad models before August 27 can receive a gift card worth up to $150. Consumers in participating states can also enjoy a limited-time sales tax holiday.

Although the back-to-school deals are exciting, the use of phones during class is becoming increasingly unpopular.

Featured comment posted by GreenPizza

I have never seen any data supporting the claim that allowing students to use phones during school shootings reduces risk. In fact, reducing classroom distractions is what truly allows us to achieve the purpose of learning.

A new Pew Research Center survey found that 77% of American adults support banning middle and high school students from using phones in class, up from 68% in 2024 and 74% in 2025. Only 18% now oppose such bans on campus.

Support for a stricter "all-day ban"—prohibiting students from using phones on campus throughout the entire day—has risen even more significantly. For the first time, more Americans support an all-day ban than oppose it.

The report also noted that younger adults remain less enthusiastic about classroom bans and all-day bans, but support has risen across all age groups since 2024. The full report can be read here.

What do you think? Should schools require students to use iPhones only during class, implement an all-day ban, or leave the decision to students and parents? Share your thoughts in the comments.
